transcript.text: I need to flag an important finding from my collateral review this week. Of the $10,000,000 in receivables reported on the borrowing-base report, $1,500,000 are invoices owed by entities under the borrower's common ownership. Our policy excludes related-party receivables, which leaves exactly $8,500,000 in truly eligible receivables. Applying the 80% advance rate, the maximum commitment we can support is $6,800,000 — well below the requested $8,000,000. I should also note that an approved renewal at this risk level requires a monthly borrowing-base certificate. I have not yet entered this finding into the credit system.

transcript.text: I have an important update from a customer call this morning. The manufacturer confirmed they must retain at least $2,000,000 of undrawn availability for a seasonal payroll contract. Additionally, the borrower has agreed to pay down exactly $500,000 before the renewal is funded. I recorded this in my client notes, which haven't yet been circulated to credit. This is critical context for sizing the facility — if we set the commitment at $6,800,000 as Victor suggests, the $500,000 paydown would bring the drawn balance to $4,500,000, leaving only $2,300,000 of undrawn availability, which is just above their $2,000,000 minimum requirement. This is tight but workable, and we should factor it into the final terms.
